// A checker or a testing.TB copied into another name is the same object, and
// `alias := c` has neither a written type nor a qt.New for the classification
// pass to read. Every violation here is one an ordinary alias used to hide,
// and every alias below is resolved at the position its initializer is written.
package fixture

import (
	"testing"

	qt "github.com/frankban/quicktest"
)

type runner struct{}

func (runner) Run(name string, f func(t *testing.T)) {
	f(nil)
}

func TestAliasedChecker(t *testing.T) {
	c := qt.New(t)
	alias := c

	t.Run("asserts through an alias of the parent checker", func(t *testing.T) {
		alias.Assert(1, qt.Equals, 1)
	})
}

func TestAliasedTB(t *testing.T) {
	parent := t

	t.Run("reads an alias of the parent TB", func(t *testing.T) {
		parent.Log("this belongs to the parent test")
	})
}

func TestAliasChain(t *testing.T) {
	c := qt.New(t)
	first := c
	second := first

	t.Run("asserts through the second link of the chain", func(t *testing.T) {
		second.Assert(2, qt.Equals, 2)
	})
}

func TestAliasedCheckerRunMethodValue(t *testing.T) {
	c := qt.New(t)
	alias := c

	run := alias.Run
	run("child", func(c *qt.C) {
		c.Assert(3, qt.Equals, 3)
	})
}

// The target shape, and two things that are not violations: an alias the
// closure declares itself is the closure's own checker, and an alias of a
// value that shadows the checker is that value, whatever the outer scope calls
// it.
func TestAliasDeclaredInsideTheSubtest(t *testing.T) {
	t.Run("the alias is the closure's own checker", func(t *testing.T) {
		c := qt.New(t)
		alias := c
		alias.Assert(4, qt.Equals, 4)
	})
}

func TestAliasOfAShadowingValue(t *testing.T) {
	c := qt.New(t)
	c.Assert(5, qt.Equals, 5)

	{
		c := runner{}
		alias := c
		alias.Run("not a quicktest subtest", func(t *testing.T) {
			t.Log("work")
		})
	}
}
